text:
Lane Hutson won the Calder in 2024-25 and then, by Evolving-Hockey's count, was the most valuable defenseman in the league last season: 4.9 wins, 1st among 215. This season Montreal is leaning on him harder still. He averages 25.1 minutes and played 27 or more in three of his last six games.

His 19 points (3 goals, 16 assists) carry almost no luck. He has 3 goals on 3.0 expected goals (the quality of his chances), the team's finishing with him on is right at expectation, and his last ten games produced 9 points against the 9.1 we'd expect. All nine were assists.

The process is the reason. At five on five the Canadiens take 56.4% of the expected goals with him on, 10.4 points better than without him. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 54% of his entries, and carry-ins led to a chance 25% of the time against 8% for dump-ins.

There is a second Hutson story now: brother Cole leads all NHL rookies in scoring for Washington, per RMNB. Lane remains the one Montreal can't take off the ice.
